mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[2.2, 1.45, 0.28])
mass void = courtyard(base, margin_ratio=0.22, open_side="west")
mass gate = lift(void, rise_ratio=0.34, support_ratio=0.18)
mass result = carve_void(gate, margin_ratio=0.12, open_side="west")
programs.name: p01_courtyard_slab_gate
programs.rationale: A grounded slab with a central court and lifted public threshold; the topology is base -> void -> lifted void, distinct from tower or split forms.

programs.dsl:
mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[2.8, 0.62, 0.48])
mass bar = bend(base, axis="y", angle_degrees=24, subdivisions=4)
mass spine = cantilever(bar, start_ratio=0.62, vector=[0.18, 0.0, 0.22])
mass result = union(spine)
programs.name: p02_bent_bar_walkway
programs.rationale: A single elongated bar is bent into a gentle urban sweep, then nudged into a modest overhang; this is a one-directional continuous mass rather than an enclosed or stacked composition.

programs.dsl:
mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[1.55, 1.15, 0.62])
mass wing = split_wing(base, axis="x", gap_ratio=0.22, bridge=true, height_ratio=0.78, ground_spine=true)
mass result = bridge(wing, wing, width=0.26, height_ratio=0.28, z=0.18)
programs.name: p03_split_wing_bridge
programs.rationale: Two wings are separated to create a legible passage and reconnect with a small bridge; the operator tree is bifurcation plus span, not carving or terrace logic.

programs.dsl:
mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[0.68, 0.68, 2.5])
mass tower = tapered_tower(base, axis="z", start_scale=[1.0, 1.0], end_scale=[0.72, 0.72], subdivisions=5)
mass plinth = attach_volume(tower, box(width=1.1, depth=0.78, height=0.34, center=true))
mass result = twist(plinth, axis="z", angle_degrees=10, subdivisions=3)
programs.name: p04_tapered_tower_plinth
programs.rationale: A vertical tower seed is tapered and given a low plinth attachment, producing a clear hierarchy of base and shaft with a restrained rotational finish.

programs.dsl:
mass profile = extruded_polygon(points=[[0.0, 0.0], [1.5, 0.0], [1.85, 0.45], [1.5, 0.9], [0.0, 0.9]], divisions=5, height=0.42)
mass hall = profiled_hall(profiled_hall, section_family="ridge", span_axis="x", section_controls=[[0.0, 0.0], [0.35, 0.18], [0.7, 0.0]])
mass result = courtyard(hall, margin_ratio=0.14, open_side="west")
programs.name: p05_profiled_hall_court
programs.rationale: An explicit profiled prism seed drives a hall-like sectioned volume, then a court is cut to establish market-like interior-public space; this is section-led rather than solid-led.

mass base = scale(unit, vector=[1.38, 1.12, 0.52])
mass step = stepped_mass(base, direction="x", levels=4, setback_ratio=0.14, shift_per_level=[0.08, 0.0, 0.0])

programs.rationale: A compact block is first stepped along one axis and then terraced along the other, creating a layered section profile instead of a single void or curve.

programs.dsl:
mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[2.0, 1.18, 0.34])
mass cross = cross_mass(base, angle_degrees=28)
mass pierced = puncture(cross, axis="z", count=4, ratio=0.14, n=2)
mass result = cut_corner(pierced, corner="ne", ratio=0.16, distance=0.12)
programs.name: p07_cross_mass_punctured
programs.rationale: A cross-shaped aggregation is punctured for light and entry, then clipped at one corner for a more urban edge; the figure is axial and perforated rather than courtyarded or split.

programs.dsl:
mass unit = box(1, 1, 1)
mass base = scale(unit, vector=[0.76, 0.76, 2.3])
mass lean = leaning_tower(base, direction="y", amount=0.26)
mass slice = slice(lean, normal=[0.0, 1.0, 0.0], offset_ratio=0.18, keep_side="front")
mass result = subtract(slice, cylinder(radius=0.16, height=1.0, center=true))
programs.name: p08_leaning_tower_slice
programs.rationale: A leaning vertical mass is sectioned to create a directional profile, then lightly subtracted to introduce a clean vertical notch; the topology is singular and asymmetrical.
